title: .config/ianf-repo-tools.toml, version 1
description: How work reaches the trunk, whether repo-fix leaves it alone, and where origin is published, for repo-list and repo-fix. Each worktree goes by its own copy, as it is on disk; the trunk's integration is the copy committed on the trunk. See repo-tools' README.

version.description: The version of this file's format.

integration.description: How a branch's work reaches the trunk. direct: landed on the trunk by hand, and only the trunk pushed. pr-rebase: by pull request, branches rebased onto the trunk. pr-merge: by pull request, the trunk merged into branches.

skip-fix.description: Whether repo-fix leaves the worktree alone, while repo-list still reports what needs attention. False when left out.

remotes.description: Each remote's git host, by the remote's name. Only origin for now. repo-fix publishes a repository with no remote on origin's git host, asking for one when it's left out, and repo-list reports an origin that isn't on it, or a remote on a repository kept local.

git-host.description: The git host origin is on. github: published with `github publish`, under the account gh is logged in as. bitbucket: with `bitbucket publish`, in bitbucket.workspace from repo-tools' config.toml. none: kept on this computer only, never published nor asked for a git host, which needs integration = "direct".
